Subject: Proposal and ask — limited-time pricing + warranty language

Alex — thanks for a productive call this morning. Attached is the updated Master Agreement and the commercial summary (StellarGrid_MA-Proposal_v3.pdf). Two asks from our side to get to signature this week: 1) a promotional discount of 30% on list for year-one ARR (customer is asking for this as part of their competitive evaluation), and 2) a limited carve-out to the standard warranty clause — they want warranty remedies greater than our usual "as-is" language.

I have looped in our deal desk (Marissa) and legal (Laura) for quick alignment. If we can get executive clearance for the commercial concession and the proposed warranty change, we can finalize the SOW and send the DocuSign link by Friday.

Deal highlights: 12-month initial term, expected first-year ARR $1.2M, expected start date Aug 1.

Attachments: StellarGrid_MA-Proposal_v3.pdf

Thanks Ben — quick internal note before we loop leadership. Summary of open items that will need exec clearance:
- Customer asking 30% off list for year one (standard playbook allows up to 20% without VP approval)
- Warranty language: customer requests a 90-day return/repair remedy and a commitment to uptime SLAs tied to service credits; our standard warranty is limited and disclaims consequential damages.
- Liability cap: customer explicitly asked us to remove the aggregate liability cap; legal will propose a higher cap rather than removal.

Laura — can you confirm redline recommendations and whether we can offer a $2M cap or a cap tied to 12 months of fees? Also, if legal can authorize up to 20% discount, we can push the customer to accept that quickly. Anything above that needs Vivek's sign-off.

If Laura sends a short redline summary, I will prepare an exec note for Vivek with the commercial tradeoffs (ACV impact vs. strategic value). Ben, please include any competitive pressure context and any committed timeline the customer gave.

Subject: Re: Proposal and ask — limited-time pricing + warranty language (redlines attached)

Team — I reviewed the latest MA and prepared a redline summary (SG_Redlines.docx). Key recommendations (summary):
- Liability cap: do not remove. Recommend $2,000,000 aggregate cap OR 12 months of fees, whichever is LOWER (limits exposure while tying to real economic value).
- Indemnity: narrow to claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; decline broad third-party IP indemnity that is uncapped.
- Warranty: we can accept a limited uptime commitment for the managed service with service credits capped at a small percentage of monthly fees, but we should refuse a remedy that includes system-wide rollback or unlimited remediation. Insert "AS-IS" warranty language with an exception for gross negligence.

Commercial concessions: Legal can pre-authorize up to 20% promotional discount for strategic early-adopter customers provided the customer signs a 12-month committed ARR and allows public case study language. Anything above 20% requires VP approval.

I recommend Marissa include these bullets in the executive ask. If leadership wants a larger discount/waiver of liability, we should require a contract amendment and an insurance check.

Attachment: SG_Redlines.docx (redline highlights and suggested language)

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Quick update: customer pushed back — they are insisting on 30% and are asking that the liability cap be removed entirely, citing procurement pressure from their board. They said it's an RFP condition for the incumbent to be eliminated. They also want full warranty remediation (including rollback) for critical incidents.

I've attached a one-page commercial impact file (updated-MAPricing.xlsx) showing margin at 20%, 25%, 30% discounts. They are at our doorstep for a quick decision and have given a soft deadline of EOD Thursday for signature to make their board cycle.

Requesting escalation: if leadership can approve 25% (with $2M liability cap and the warranty as Laura proposed), we can close this quarter and protect the relationship. If leadership will not move on cap, we will lose the deal to a competitor that is offering broader terms.

Team — thanks for the clear summary and the financials. I will approve the following, contingent on the customer signing the 12-month committed ARR SOW and accepting a public case study within 6 months:
1) Promotional discount of 25% for year one only (not to be extended without VP review).
2) Liability cap set at $2,000,000 aggregate OR 12 months of fees, whichever is LOWER.
3) Indemnity narrowed per Laura's language (gross negligence/willful misconduct carve-out only).
4) Warranty to be "AS-IS" with service credits as the exclusive remedy (no rollback or unlimited remediation).

Marissa — please prepare the exec approval memo and route to Finance for final credit checks and to Legal for inclusion of the redline language. Ben — execute the updated commercial sheet and send the DocuSign link once DocuSign is prepared.

This is a one-time exception based on strategic risk/reward. Any deviation from the above must come back to me.

Vivek Kulkarni
